{{Quote|But the tales I've told these little people! I've regaled with details of every evil deed you have committed, and more than a few you haven't. The warriors want to cut you down right now, but Elder Alexem here wants to give you a chance. So you'd better explain to the silly old geezer why they shouldn't kill you.|Kelyan|<ref name="Strike III" />}}
'''Alexem''' was the elder of a [[City/Legends|village]] of [[Squib/Legends|Squibs]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Holador]]. His tribe was descended from a group of Squibs who crash-landed on the world circa [[221 BBY]] and had since adopted a primitive lifestyle. Alexem was a respected member of the tribe, the protector of its Holy Icon&mdash;a nonfunctional [[Comm unit/Legends|comms relay]]&mdash;and a resolver of his tribe's disputes.

In [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]], a [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Gender/Legends|woman]] named [[Kelyan]] appeared in the village with tales of a band of evil offworlders who were close behind her. While the village [[Soldier/Legends|warriors]] itched to defend their loved ones, Alexem urged caution and sent warriors to invite the strangers to come and explain their presence to him. Once they arrived, Alexem weighed both parties' stories. He declared that the Twi'lek had been lying and that the outsiders were to be treated as guests before letting them continue on their way unmolested.

==Biography==
{{Quote|Good grief, more off-worlders. I better go tell the boss.|A Squib scout|<ref name="Strike III" />}}
Alexem was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Squib/Legends|Squib]] born in a primitive [[City/Legends|village]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Holador]]. His people were descended from Squib [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]] who survived their [[Unidentified Squib vessel|vessel's]] crash-landing on the world circa [[221 BBY]]. Despite their [[Distress beacon/Legends|distress signals]], no rescue came for the survivors, and their technology slowly failed. Over seven generations, they adapted to primitive living conditions and learned to eke out an existence by hunting and gathering. That they would someday be saved from their lot by people from the [[Star/Legends|stars]] became an intrinsic part of their mythology. Technological items were recycled for more basic purposes, and the [[Comm unit/Legends|comms relay]] came to be seen as a Holy Icon. Alexem was one of the last Squibs in his tribe to retain knowledge of [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]], and he rose to be the elder of the 50-Squib village in the later days of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="Strike III" />

In [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]], an outsider appeared, a [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] named [[Kelyan]]. At first, the Squibs were skittish around her, but she spoke [[Squibbian]] and used it to regale the tribe with the exploits of her companions and their battle with a group she referred to as the [[Assassin/Legends|Assassin]] [[Lord/Legends|Lords]] and their minions. The villagers slowly came to trust the stranger, even to like her, but Alexem was not so sure of her intentions. There was something about her that he did not like, and he hid his ability to speak Basic from her. He thought it better to hear both sides of the debate before making up his mind.<ref name="Strike III" />

{{RPG}}
Some days later, a [[Scout/Legends|scout]] returned from the tunnels neighboring the village with news of another group of offworlders. Kelyan warned that these were the evil beings whose misdeeds she had been recounting, and the edgy Squib [[Soldier/Legends|warriors]] called out for the strangers' [[Blood/Legends|blood]]. Nevertheless, Alexem ordered a group of warriors to find these outsiders, invite them to the village, and escort them back to the Squibs' home. Alexem did not intend to treat the outsiders with violence&mdash;unless they proved the woman's story to be correct.<ref name="Strike III" />

That evening, the warriors returned with the so-called villains in tow, and the Twi'lek woman chided them for their supposed misdeeds. The village warriors seemed more on edge than ever, but Alexem ordered them to hold off. Revealing his knowledge of Basic, he told the outsiders to explain who they were and what they were doing on Holador. A bitter back-and-forth ensued with the Twi'lek and the strangers arguing for their respective innocence and the other side's duplicity. In particular, the group of strangers claimed to have crash-landed on Holador as part of an elaborate trap set by the Twi'lek and her companions, a band of [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]] who were trying to kill them.<ref name="Strike III" />

Alexem weighed both sides' words carefully and came to his decision: The outsiders appeared to mean no harm to his people, so they would be allowed to leave in peace. He decided that his village would even aid them in whatever way they required. As for Kelyan, Alexem declared that despite her mendacity, she was a guest of the village and had not actually broken any of the tribal laws.<ref name="Strike III" />
{{Endgame}}

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|I listen true.|Alexem|<ref name="Strike III" />}}
Alexem was old for his species. During village business, he sat in a decrepit flight chair near the fire pit at the center of the village with the Holy Icon to his back. The elder wrapped himself in thick blankets that left only his [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] and ears visible. He was wise and patient, calming his warriors' tempers and insisting on hearing both sides of a dispute before coming to a decision. Alexem spoke Basic, albeit imperfectly: his accent was thick and his command of vocabulary and usage were far from perfect.<ref name="Strike III" />

==Behind the scenes==
Alexem appears in ''[[For Every Action: Strike III|Strike III]]'', an adventure for the [[Living Force/Legends|''Living Force'']] campaign of the ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]'' from [[Wizards of the Coast]] that was released in [[2005]]. The Squib and his village are part of an encounter in which the player characters are expected to rely on roleplaying and non-combat abilities to advance their quest. Meanwhile, they must contend with Kelyan, who is doing her best to convince Alexem and his tribe that the player characters are dangerous and should not be allowed to leave the village alive.<ref name="Strike III" />

In an encounter with a Squib scout from Alexem's village, the player characters may react cautiously and amicably, or they may treat the scout aggressively. Should they choose force and intimidation, Alexem's warriors attack them rather than escort them to the village. The scenario considers fighting to be the wrong course of action, however, and penalizes such behavior by pushing such characters further toward the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]].<ref name="Strike III" />

Once at the village, the outcome of the encounter depends on players making good die rolls and thinking of ways to curry favor with the elder and the Squibs, such as offering technological items, rations, or medical assistance. Should they do poorly, the Squib warriors attack. Success means that Alexem and his companions decide that the outsiders are in fact harmless and befriend them. As the best possible outcome, this is considered the [[canon]]ical path.<ref name="Strike III" />
